Lina (support): Customer dropped a 12s screen recording of the error — link: https://files.example.com/zoom_rec_1234.mp4. They said the console prints a 'request token' at ~0:03 but couldn't copy it. Any quick extraction suggestions? :wave:
Sam (eng-oncall): If they can upload the MP4 we can extract a single frame at the time the console shows the token. Ask them for the approximate second and whether the console text is readable.
Lina (support): Asked for the timestamp, customer replied 'around 3s, maybe 3.1s'. They sent the MP4.
Sam (eng-oncall): Perfect. Quick command we ask them (or we can run on the file):
Sam (eng-oncall): ```
ffmpeg -i zoom_rec_1234.mp4 -ss 00:00:03.100 -vframes 1 frame_003.png
```
Sam (eng-oncall): That will give a still frame we can zoom/crop. If the token is small, crop it with ImageMagick: `convert frame_003.png -crop 1200x200+300+600 cropped.png` then run OCR: `tesseract cropped.png out -l eng --psm 6`
Priya (mobile SDK): If it's from a mobile webview, the token might be in an `x-rw-session` or `x-rw-req` header in the network panel. Ask them to: open devtools (or proxy), reproduce, and copy the network request headers. That is usually easiest.
Lina (support): Customer doesn't know devtools. They're non-technical and only have the video.
Sam (eng-oncall): Ok — OCR is the fallback. A couple of heuristics for the token pattern we look for when scanning OCR output:
Sam (eng-oncall): - hex-ish session: `[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}`
Sam (eng-oncall): - short alphanumeric request refs: `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}`
Priya (mobile SDK): Also check for visible header names like `x-rw-session`, `x-session`, `reqref`, `request-id` around the token in the screenshot. If you can crop a little more context it helps disambiguate.
Lina (support): Run OCR and paste the raw output here once you have it, we'll grep for likely candidates.
DebugBot: Uploaded file processing started (ffmpeg -> frame extraction queued).
Sam (eng-oncall): If OCR yields multiple candidates, tell customer to blur/hide other parts and re-send a higher-resolution screenshot focused on the console.
Lina (support): OCR output: `ERROR: request failed\nrequest token: a1b2c3d4-56ef-78ab-90cd-1234ef567890\nstack: ...`
Priya (mobile SDK): That `a1b2c3d4-56ef-78ab-90cd-1234ef567890` looks like a session/req token. Can you ask customer to also send the exact wall-clock time (e.g., 2025-07-05T14:03:12Z) and the endpoint they hit? That helps us correlate in logs.
Lina (support): Asked for timestamp and endpoint; customer said `2025-07-05 14:03:12 UTC` and `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Sam (eng-oncall): Great — with token + timestamp + endpoint we can search logs. If we still can't find it, ask for a short HAR or a minimal curl they can run:
Sam (eng-oncall): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token_or_session_here>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Priya (mobile SDK): For mobile customers who can't run curl, ask them to share a device screenshot of the app settings -> about -> version + any console lines. Even app version + timestamp often narrows the search significantly.
Lina (support): Customer sent the requested time and endpoint and asked if we can redact the token after use. I confirmed we'll only use it for debugging and will redact in notes. :lock_with_ink_pen:
Sam (eng-oncall): Quick internal note for correlation: if you search logs use a time window +/- 2 minutes around the provided timestamp and grep for either the full token or the last 8 characters (sometimes tokens are truncated in screenshots). Also check proxy edge logs for `req-ref` fields.
Priya (mobile SDK): If this becomes a recurring pain point, we should add a small UI helper in the console: 'Copy request token' button visible in debug mode. Filing a follow-up ticket.
Lina (support): Thanks all — I ran the grep and found the request id in our logs, attached the trace id to the ticket and requested a debug bundle from eng for root cause. Customer happy with workaround for now. :thumbsup:
